writeup: TIC 290436243 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.0793 days, showing a primary eclipse that dims the system by 3.35 percent. The signal was detected in TESS photometry with a box-least-squares significance of 113.0. Pixel-level image analysis found a peak signal-to-noise of 24.8, though the centroid offset measures 3.2 arcseconds from the target. No secondary eclipse was detected. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, a significant uncertainty remains: the pixel-level analysis places the dimming centroid only 0.071 pixels closer to the target than to a nearby bright star, falling within TESS's documented centroid uncertainty of 0.10-0.3 pixels, meaning the two stars cannot be confidently separated at this resolution.
